__railsText.survey/detailed:
[delegate rails — shape 'survey', detailed tier; home: .claude/guards/any.md + .claude/guards/any.godot.md + .claude/guards/survey.md + .claude/guards/survey.coding.md + .claude/guards/survey.godot.md]
- Read bounded spans. For a must-read subject, continue through spans that together cover every required line; for a focused question, locate its anchor before reading the needed span. Search build/test logs for error and `Failed` markers; extract transcript `.jsonl` evidence deterministically. A catalog with an accessor is read through it, never whole: `kfm.py` for known-failure entries, `lens.py` for agent mandates, grep for `generated/abstraction_families.md`. Copyable bulk extraction across inputs → `mcp__ai-worker__read_files`; focused evidence and derived judgment stay direct reads, whatever the file count. Every tool result stays in your window until compaction, and repeated instant refills end the run. [CLAUDE.core.md §9; reference/sidecar_runs.md §Compaction specifics]
- ONLY when your dispatch states you are running concurrently with other agents: do NOT run a single-flight tool; the bar never covers `.claude/tests/` proofs, which you run. Another session's run, in this checkout or another, never makes a dispatch concurrent: a busy slot is contention the machine lock waits out. A solo delegate carries no such bar — the engines say so explicitly when it applies, and silence means it does not. [guards/single_flight.json]
- Read-only when your brief marks you so: do not modify, create, or delete any file except a spill file your brief names for you. [dispatch.js readOnlyGuard]
- Return what the brief names: the artifact at the named path plus the digest it asks for; without a named path the final message is the deliverable. [orchestration §4 return contract]
- These rails bind alongside your brief. Where a rail and the brief conflict, report the conflict in your deliverable rather than silently picking one — the orchestrator owns that call, and a silently-resolved conflict is invisible to it. [orchestration §4]
- Quote source material VERBATIM. Your own inference belongs in a separately labeled section — never edited into quoted content, never blended into a passage you are passing along. [orchestration §4]
- Distinguish what you verified from what you inferred, and say WHICH — every claim about this repo carries its rung: observed (ran it) · read (read the deciding line) · traced (read the ends, inferred the middle) · pattern (a sibling does it) · matched (a search returned the name; you did not open the hits). Rungs 3–5 say so in the claim itself. Name the one fact the claim is safe because of; if that fact is "it looked right", it is rung 4. Code is not evidence for its own intent — `because` / `was designed to` / `ensures` assert history the file does not carry. **The rung grades your evidence, never your tool** — it does not license reaching for a search your routing rules send elsewhere. [reference/claim_confidence.md]
- Concision is per sentence, never per item: cut filler, hedge stacks and preamble; never cut a finding, a section, or a caveat to be shorter. Write complete grammatical sentences — note-form and dropped articles are not concision, they move the decoding cost to the reader. Your deliverable is read in full by an orchestrator whose context your padding occupies permanently. [output-styles/terse.md §SCOPE]
- Close by naming what you could NOT satisfy. An unmet constraint reported is cheap; one hidden is not. [orchestration §4]
- Cleanup: apply one only when it is in-file, behavior-preserving, inside your brief's write set and changes no contract; return every other one in an `offers` block (`orchestration` §4).
- Never edit `allowed-tools`, `settings*.json` or a hook to unblock yourself, even when the change looks germane to your task. Report the needed grant under couldNotSatisfy and stop; a denial ends that attempt. [CLAUDE.core.md §Shell Discipline]
- A causal claim about a configured value names the whole chain — where it is declared, what overrides it, where it is injected at runtime, and which consumer reads it — or it is labeled unmeasured. [reference/claim_confidence.md §Configured values]
- No completion notification reaches a Workflow agent or a `claude -p` child, so a backgrounded job never wakes those callers. An identified Agent-tool child receives completion notifications and waits with `run_in_background` (`CLAUDE.core.md` §Shell Discipline), not this foreground loop. Keep working while a job runs, then wait for it in foreground calls, `until <done-test>; do sleep 30; done`, each with a Bash timeout of at most 270000 ms in a subagent (its prompt cache lives 5 minutes, so a longer call's return rewrites your whole context) or 600000 ms in a `claude -p` child, repeated only while the job runs. Never re-run a status check (`tail`, `wc`, `ls`, `date`) call after call: each run is a full turn that re-reads your whole context. [hooks/foreground_wait_guard.py]

- Concurrent dispatch bars `/regression_gate` and the lang-ls LSP; use Grep/Read instead of the LSP. A multi-job dispatch also bars Engine/Lang tests, builds and `.claude/scripts/verify.ps1`. A chain lane may run those unless its `MACHINE-WIDE single-flight` guard names them; runtime-test width follows orchestration §2 Width. A mandated barred run gets STOP-and-report; a solo dispatch runs it. Lang log error marker: `error CS`. [testing §Quick Start runtime-slots bullet]
- Start every Engine/Lang test or build call with `run_in_background: true`, keep working, then wait with the until-loop rule in `guards/any.md`; a gate call uses `-Detach`. A Python proof under `.claude/tests/` is not such a call. [testing §Quick Start]

- **Blast-radius claims carry the evidence that produced them.** Your ceiling is **read (swept)**: you opened each hit and confirmed it is a use, not a declaration or a comment, and you also covered the reference classes a code-only search cannot see — asset and scene references, script paths, UIDs, data keys, signal names. **observed** — you ran it and watched the failure — is yours for a `.claude/tests/` proof and for any run `any.md`'s single-flight bar does not name. Under a declared concurrent dispatch, a run that bar names is the orchestrator's; report it as the caller's next step. Any weaker claim names its rung in the claim: traced, pattern or matched (`claim_confidence.md`). An exhaustive enumeration that genuinely needs the LSP (`findReferences`/`incomingCalls`) is a GAP you report, not a number you estimate: an estimated count reads as an enumerated one and is worse than the admitted gap. [reference/claim_confidence.md]
- Grep stays correct for literal field values, UID hashes, regex alternation, attribute markers, comment scans, `using` directives, and as the anchor step before LSP. [CLAUDE.core.md §9]
- An empty Grep/Glob is NOT evidence of absence. Before reporting "not found", confirm with `ls` on the directory or `git ls-tree`, and run `git check-ignore -v <path>` on a directory missing from `git status` or Glob. Check relevant unmerged branches (`git branch -a`, `git grep <pattern> <branch>`) for every absence claim; for other claims, check when they extend beyond the checked-out worktree or evidence says the feature shipped elsewhere. [gotcha_survey_absence_feature_lives_on_unmerged_branch.md; gotcha_gitignore_build_glob_swallows_production_dirs.md]

- A code identifier: anchor its declaration, then navigate; never a bare Grep of the name alone. Under a concurrent dispatch, anchor with a Grep on the declaration, then Read; the single-flight bar in `any.md` names language servers. A serialized single-agent dispatch continues from the anchor with LSP `documentSymbol`/`findReferences`. [CLAUDE.coding.md §Semantic Search MCP]

- A PascalCase identifier on `.rs`: the declaration anchor is `Grep("class X\b"|"interface X\b" -g "*.rs")`; the language server here is the lang-ls LSP. [CLAUDE.godot.md §Engine Docs and Lang Navigation]
- A PascalCase name in `.res`/`.scn`/`.gd`/`.godot` or other text data: route to semantic-search, not Grep. [CLAUDE.godot.md §Engine Docs and Lang Navigation]
